In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BK and AngII are not antagonistic in their actions, but rather that the two peptides interact in the regulation of the expression of CTGF mRNA in IMR- 90 fibroblasts.
, in these cells, AngII and BK have opposite effects on the regulation of the expression of the fibrogenic factor CTGF.
BK modulates AngII-evoked CTGF expression through a RhoA-dependent, Galphai/Galphao-independent pathway, which involves a BKB2R-AT1R interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BKB2R and AT1R are coupled to the same signaling pathway, which is the activation of the MAP kinases, but the AT1R and not the BKB2Rs are coupled to the activation of RhoA.
the opposing physiological actions between BK and AngII are mediated by a common pathway involving RhoA and CTGF expression.
the AT1R/BkB2R chimera, lacking G protein coupling, retains a signaling pathway for CTGF expression, which is not shared by the AT1R or BKB2R.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in human fibroblasts in culture, the AT1R and the BKB2R are coupled to the same signaling pathways, but the AT1R, unlike the BKB2 receptor, is coupled to RhoA, which in turn regulates the expression of CTGF mRNA.
the opposing physiological effects of BK and AngII in human lung fibrotic diseases are mediated by a signaling mechanism distinct from the one previously described in vascular smooth muscle cells.
